newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah stable in slow late trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah stable in slow late trading.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was stable against the dollar in slow late trading on Monday.
Dealers said focus was still on liquidity, but the worries seemed to ease in the afternoon, with swap and interbank rates easing from morning highs.
They said the dollar-rupiah rate was little changed after light early pressure due to liquidity concerns as banks geared up to meet the new reserve requirement rate of five percent on Wednesday.
One Japanese bank dealer said swap rates eased off after overnight and short-term money rates declined.
"There was not much activity in the afternoon. The focus is on meeting the five-percent reserve rate. We are mobilising funds to prepare for it and after Wednesday," he said.
Another dealer said banks appeared to have no problem in meeting the requirement, but operators appeared to be worried over market conditions in the aftermath.
Spot rupiah was at 2,404.50/04.75 at 0930 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,404.30/05.30. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,404.10/04.35 and 2,403.40/03.85, respectively.
Overnight money fell to nine from 12.0/12.5 percent.
Some said there were worries over possible tight conditions on Tuesday due to weekly tax payment, but it was not reflected in the overnight rate. Overnight swap closed at 0.45/0.50.
Tom/next swap was at 0.47/0.50 points. One-week swap was at 3.3/3.5. Dealers said longer-term swaps edged down following declines in overnight money.
One-month swaps edged down to 12.5/13.0 from 13.00/13.75, two to 25.0/26.5 from 26.0/27.0, three to 37.0/38.0 from 38.0/38.5 and six to 73.0/74.0 from 73.50/74.25.
Bank Indonesia raised its intervention band by one point to 2,400/2,592 and the conversion band to 2,400/2,448 on Monday.
